title: Dedicated burst credit aggregation and billing reconciliation for reserved throughput
creator: Ava Morgan
description:
Problem: Customers on Dedicated pools purchase reserved throughput (units/sec) and are allowed short bursts beyond the reservation. Current meter logic attributes every token/request beyond the reservation to immediate overage without properly aggregating burst consumption, leading to incorrect billing and SLA credit calculation. We have observed two concrete failures: (1) short, repeated sub-second bursts from multi-tenant routing causing large instantaneous counters; (2) race conditions in the meter writer that double-counts transient KV-cache evictions. Both produce overcharge and poor SLA credit signals.

Goal: Implement deterministic burst credit aggregation, correct rate-limit enforcement, and a reconciled billing view for reserved throughput that drives both invoicing and SLA credit calculations. Implementation must be auditable, support backfill/reconciliation for historical windows, and preserve low-latency path for request admission control.
acceptance_criteria: Burst usage is aggregated into a time-windowed credit bucket per pool (configurable window, default 60s)
Invoices reflect aggregated burst consumption rather than instantaneous peak overshoot for all test accounts in the sandbox environment
SLA credit triggers match post-reconciliation signals (manual test: intentionally throttle a pool to validate credit issuance)
No more than 0.1% additional tail latency introduced on admission checks in the dedicated path
Reconciliation job provides delta reports and an audit log for every adjustment and flagging of retro credits
technical_notes:
Design decisions: use event-sourced meter writes into a compact append-only table (meter_events) with dedupe by (request_id OR idempotency_key). Aggregation will run in two layers: (A) admission-time fast path: check token-bucket using in-memory sliding-window counters keyed by pool_id and shard; accept/soft-reject based on reserve+local burst token count. This path must be best-effort and idempotent. (B) periodic aggregator: windowed rollup job (default 60s tumbling windows) will consume meter_events via a materialized streaming read (postgres logical replication or Kafka) and write reconciled consumption to billing_aggregates table. Reconciliation job computes: reserved_consumption, aggregated_burst, burst_apportionment_by_customer, and suggested_sla_credit.

Edge cases & trade-offs: We can keep admission-time checks stateless (faster) but must accept eventual reconciliation corrections (may require retro credits). Alternatively, maintain a globally consistent admission counter at cost of ~5-10ms increased latency; we chose eventual correctness with a small reconciliation window to keep p95 latency targets.

Schema notes (proposal): meter_events(columns): event_id, pool_id, pool_shard, timestamp, request_id, customer_id, tokens_consumed, event_type, metadata_json, writer_node_id. billing_aggregates(columns): window_start, pool_id, reserved_tokens, aggregated_burst_tokens, reconciled_at, reconciliation_source.

Idempotency: meter_event writers must attach request_id or idempotency_key and be retried safely. Aggregator must dedupe by event_id.

Backfill: add a backfill tool that replays historical request logs into meter_events and marks aggregate records with reconciliation_source='backfill'.
testing_plan:
1) Unit tests for meter_event dedupe and aggregator logic; 2) Integration test: synthetic workload generator (bursty traffic pattern, multi-tenant) in sandbox dedicated pool to validate invoices and SLA credit signals; 3) Load test at production throughput (sample 5M tokens/min) to confirm aggregator lag < 60s under normal load; 4) Chaos test: simulate node restarts and duplicate event writes to validate idempotency.

Test artifacts and scripts: ./tools/billing/simulate_burst.py, ./tools/billing/reconcile_smoke.sh
rollout_notes:
- Deploy meter_event writer logic behind feature-flag; start writing events in parallel with existing counters.
- Run reconciler in dry-run mode against production mirror for 48 hours and compare deltas (report to #billing-ops).
- If delta < 0.5% for top-10 customers, enable reconciler for automated adjustments (windowed).
- Schedule invoice run not to apply retro credits until finance approves adjustments for the past billing period.

Fallback: if reconciler causes >5% unexpected credit delta, flip reconciler to manual review mode and revert admission path to current conservative overage billing for new invoices.
